detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA extended the review of the NDA for a PET diagnostic kit for somatostatin receptor-positive neuroendocrine tumors, setting a new PDUFA goal date of 2026-06-29. The extension is to review additional manufacturing information and is not related to efficacy or safety data. This delays the potential timing of a regulatory decision.
catalyst_text_evidence: Lantheus Holdings, Inc. ("Lantheus" or "Company") (NASDAQ:LNTH) ... announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has extended its review of the New Drug Application (NDA) for LNTH-2501 (Gallium 68 edotreotide) by three months to 2026-06-29. The extension and revised target Prescription Drug User Free Act (PDUFA) goal date of 2026-06-29, will allow the FDA additional time to review and consider further manufacturing related information submitted by Lantheus. This standard review extension is not related to the efficacy or safety data of LNTH-2501.

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for prostate cancer imaging indication
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA approved a new formulation of the F 18 PSMA PET imaging agent for use in men with prostate cancer, including those with suspected metastasis prior to definitive therapy or suspected recurrence based on elevated PSA. The filing used the 505(b)(2) pathway referencing prior pivotal studies, providing an authorized diagnostic option for PSMA-positive lesion imaging.
catalyst_text_evidence: Lantheus… today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved PYLARIFY TruVu (piflufolastat F 18) injection, a new formulation of its F 18 prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) imaging agent. PYLARIFY TruVu is indicated for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positive lesions in men with prostate cancer with suspected metastasis who are candidates for initial definitive therapy or suspected recurrence based on elevated serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level.

catalyst_text: Received FDA tentative approval for GEP NETs indication
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA granted tentative approval to the ANDA for a radioequivalent version of lutetium Lu 177 dotatate for gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Tentative approval confirms the application meets approval requirements, though commercial launch awaits resolution of a Hatch-Waxman 30-month stay. This represents a key regulatory milestone for bringing an alternative option to patients with GEP-NETs.
catalyst_text_evidence: Lantheus Holdings, Inc. ... today announced that it has received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) tentative approval for the Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) for Lutetium Lu 177 Dotatate (PNT2003), a radioequivalent1 version of LUTATHERA® (lutetium Lu 177 dotatate). LUTATHERA® is indicated for the treatment of somatostatin receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs), including foregut, midgut, and hindgut neuroendocrine tumors. The FDA tentative approval indicates that the FDA has completed its review of the ANDA and that it meets the requirements for approval under the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetics Act. Full approval of the ANDA is subject to the expiration of the 30-month stay in June 2026, triggered in connection with a Hatch-Waxman patent litigation.
